steps.text: Get every IV Cefazolin dose on the schedule from the infectious-disease team (every scheduled dose until the course is complete)
Take Furosemide 40 mg once a day
Take Losartan 25 mg once a day
Weigh yourself every day and watch for swelling or breathlessness
Check your PICC line site every day for redness, drainage or bleeding
Get the blood tests on your outpatient antibiotic plan (as scheduled)
Go to all infectious-disease appointments (as scheduled)
Go to all cardiology (heart doctor) appointments (as scheduled)
Keep your PICC line care appointments (as scheduled)
Eat a low-salt diet and follow your fluid plan
Follow any activity limits and dental-procedure advice from your teams

medications.name: Cefazolin
medications.howOften: through your IV line, at the dose and schedule the infectious-disease team gave you
medications.why: The antibiotic that kills the valve infection. Every dose matters. Do not stop or change it on your own.

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.why: A water pill that keeps fluid from building up. You will urinate more.

medications.name: Losartan
medications.why: Helps your heart, started at a low dose because your blood pressure and kidneys are still recovering.

medications.name: Metoprolol succinate
medications.howOften: at the dose on your discharge list

medications.name: Other chronic medications
medications.howOften: as on your final medication list

medications.name: Empiric inpatient antibiotics
medications.why: Stopped. The hospital antibiotics were replaced by cefazolin, which targets your exact infection.

medications.name: NSAIDs
medications.why: Avoid pain relievers like ibuprofen unless your doctor says it is okay. They can hurt your heart and kidneys.

followUps.why: Track the antibiotic course and blood tests
Check your heart valve and heart failure plan

followUps.who: Outpatient infusion and PICC care team
followUps.why: Give the IV antibiotic and care for the line

warnings.text: New weakness, a drooping face, trouble speaking, or confusion (signs of stroke)
Sudden severe back, chest or belly pain
Fever, chills, or feeling very sick again
New or worsening shortness of breath
Swelling or weight going up quickly
Bleeding, a lot of drainage, or redness around the PICC line
Any problem with the IV line, such as it will not flush or looks damaged
Questions about your medicines after discharge
